study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Multivariate Fractional Polynomial Regression (MFPR) was used as the primary algorithm within the CentileBrain normative modeling framework. The normative models were developed using data from 37,407 healthy individuals. Sex-specific models were generated for each regional measure. Sensitivity analyses also tested GAMLSS and GPR as alternative algorithms, but MFPR was identified as the optimal algorithm through benchmarking.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In the normative modeling framework, the optimal models were defined following benchmarking of 8 different algorithms (ordinary least squares regression; bayesian linear regression; generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape; parametric λ, μ, and ς method; multivariable fractional polynomial regression; gaussian process regression; warped bayesian linear regression; and hierarchical bayesian regression)... Through this pipeline, we identified multivariable fractional polynomial regression as the optimal algorithm; We used the CentileBrain framework (https://centilebrain.org/) to generate sex-specific normative models for each of the FreeSurfer-extracted regional measure... estimated using Multivariate Fractional Polynomial Regression (MFPR)

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional measures of cortical thickness (CT; n=68 regions), cortical surface area (SA; n=68 regions), and subcortical volume (SV; n=14 regions) were derived from T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer software. These measures were used as the response variables in the normative models.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: clinical-, IQ-, and neuroimaging software (FreeSurfer)-derived regional measures of cortical thickness (CT), cortical surface area (SA), and subcortical volume (SV) from 1340 individuals with CHR-P and 1237 healthy individuals pooled from 29 international sites; Images were parcellated and segmented at each respective site using standard pipelines implemented using FreeSurfer analysis software (https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/) to yield regional measures of cortical thickness (CT), cortical surface area (SA), and subcortical volume (SV)

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Sex-specific normative models were generated (separate models for males and females). Age was the primary explanatory variable using fractional polynomial terms. Site effects were harmonized using ComBat-GAM. Model optimization included global neuroimaging features: ICV for subcortical volume models, mean cortical thickness for CT models, and mean cortical surface area for SA models.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: the optimal covariate combination involved site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) and the inclusion of intracranial volume, mean CT, and mean SA in the models of the regional measures of SV, CT, and SA, respectively; Sex-specific normative models for each neuroimaging software (FreeSurfer)-derived regional CT, SA, and SV measure were generated; models were trained using 5-fold cross-validation (5F-CV) in the corresponding sex-specific training subset with age being the only explanatory variable and then model parameters were tested in the corresponding sex-specific test subset... model optimization involves the inclusion in the models of covariates pertaining to acquisition and global neuroimaging features (i.e., ICV for SV models, mean cortical thickness for CT models and mean cortical surface area for SA models)
